blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We are about to move on to the cases of [Baby L] and [Baby M]. They are both allegations of attempted murder. I'm sure the jury will remember that in effect both events were going on pretty much at the same time, but [Baby L]'s case is one involving the alleged administration of insulin, whereas [Baby M]'s case is one that coincides more with the type of evidence that the jury have been hearing as we've been going along in many of the other cases.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: So rather than confusing the issues by presenting things strictly chronologically with things going on with either child at the same time, we are going to concentrate first on the case
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: of [Baby L], who is the insulin case, call that evidence, then call the factual evidence relating to [Baby M] and then call the expert evidence dealing with both.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Right, thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: So Kate Tyndall, please.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: MRS KATE TYNDALL (recalled)
Examination-in-chief by MR JOHNSON
Welcome back. For the recording would you identify yourself, please?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm Kate Tyndall, intelligence analyst.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Thank you, Mrs Tyndall. Can we go to the sequence -sorry.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: (Pause)
Mrs Tyndall, can we start at tile number 1 with Mr Murphy's assistance, please.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Tile 1 records the births of [Baby L] and indeed, to a degree, [Baby M]. They were twins, born by C-section on 8 April 2016.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: If we just go behind that, we see towards the middle of the text that no resuscitation was required. [Baby L] cried immediately. His Apgar scores -- essentially, he got full marks at 1, 5 and 10 minutes.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Thank you. The second tile records the birth of [Baby M]; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Then we have at 10.30, tile number 3, the admission of [Baby L] to the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: As we see from the tile itself, the two medical professionals that completed the necessary paperwork were Lucy Letby and Dr Bhowmik.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: At tile number 4, [Baby L]'s vital signs were recorded by Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Then at tile number 5, at 10.58, we have blood gas results?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At tile number 6, [Baby L] was cannulated at 11 am?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: And that is -- there's a record made by Lucy Letby concerning the fact that he was given sucrose and containment as pain management?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At tile number 7, we see Dr Bhowmik's notes of that procedure, which succeeded at the first attempt.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: At tile number 8 we have clinical notes, timed at 11.40, completed by Dr Barrett and Dr Mayberry concerning [Baby L]'s delivery and transfer?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Tile number 9 is further observations taken at noon?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Ten and 11 are the other two of what I have been calling the standard three.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Ten is actually a prescription for dextrose.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Quite right. Eleven is the fluid balance chart, completed by Lucy Letby.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Then at 12 are some further clinical notes made by Dr Bhowmik. You have helpfully annotated on the tile itself the fact that at this very early stage [Baby L] had low blood sugar.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Tile 13 is Lucy Letby's nursing note and I'd like to look at that if we can, please. Can you take us through what she recorded?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. This is an extract from the full summary notes she wrote at 17.42, dealing with the low blood sugar. So she writes:
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: "Initial blood sugar shortly after birth, 1.9 micromoles. Advised by Reg Bhowmik to commence 10% glucose at 3ml/kg/hour and give 60ml/kilogram/day of donor-expressed breast milk. Myself and shift leader A Davies have discussed this with Reg Bhowmik as does not follow the hypoglycaemic pathway."
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Thank you. At 14 there is a prescription?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: That's also timed at noon. Tile 15, at 12.14 hours, further blood gases?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: By this stage, according to the blood gas, the blood sugar level had risen to 2.5?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: So that's 14 minutes after the previous blood gas.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: At 16, a pathology sample, a venous blood sample taken for a blood culture?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Which revealed nothing after 5 days?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Tile 17, timed at 12.37, a further blood sample?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: If one were to go behind the tile, we'd see what the results were. Sorry, I wasn't inviting that. I think we're all familiar with these sort of things and insofar as they are relevant we'll deal with them with the medics.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Tile 18, further observations at 13.00 hours together with the neonatal fluid balance chart at the same time at tile 19?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: We then come to some text or WhatsApp messages; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, these are just a collection of messages between -this first one is between [Nurse E] and [Nurse A], a collection of them.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Yes. You've recorded -- if we just click on the tile itself, we'll see that between 11.13 hours and 12.09 hours, there are incoming and outgoing messages involving work between Lucy Letby, [Nurse A] and [Nurse E], but none of them mention [Baby L].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At 21, at 12.28 hours, [Nurse A] sent a message to Lucy Letby. Could you take us through its contents, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: She writes:
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: "Only if you get chance could you let me know who is in management and ward wise on Tuesday. I feel crap. Like a failure. Like I'm letting you all down."
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Just to put this in context, this is a Friday, so requesting information for 4 days later?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At tile 22, Lucy Letby responded at 13.05.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes:
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: "GP signed you off? I haven't had chance to look, it's mad. Don't feel like that, it can't be helped, and you've got to put yourself first and get yourself well."
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Almost immediately did [Nurse E] then send a message to Lucy Letby saying:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Oh how sad. How's your day going today? Did you make it to salsa?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Lucy Letby responded to that, is that right, 2 minutes later?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, reading:
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: "Baby has stomas now. It's busy! [Nurse A] been signed off till end of month and unit full so struggling for staff. All fun and games! Yeah, went to salsa [smiley emoji]. Been to water park yet?"
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Thank you. The next time is number 25, timed at 13.30, and this is Lucy Letby's record of her communication with [Parents of Babies L & M]; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Can you take us through what she recorded at that time?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Parents were shown babies in theatre and had a quick cuddle. I updated parents on CLS [I think that's central labour suite]. Consent given for donor milk. Aware of need for phototherapy, antibiotics and IV fluids. Photographs given and visiting hours discussed. Daddy visited the unit and had cuddles."
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Thank you. Next is 26, timed at 14.00 hours. Is that further observations of [Baby L]'s vital signs?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Followed at 27, at the same time, by the neonatal fluid balance chart?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: And at 28 by Dr Bhowmik's record of a communication that she had -- Dr Bhowmik had had with the [Surname of Babies L & M] parents --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: -- or at least [Father of Babies L & M]? Does that read:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Updated dad on NNU at about 14.00. Explained re increased fluids to stabilise sugars and plan to introduce enteral feeds. Donor-expressed breast milk consent obtained. Twin 2 needing phototherapy, jaundice, hence twin 1 also on IV antibiotics for possible infection."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Does tile 29 record the fact that there were various social messages being exchanged between 13.08 hours and 14.39?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: And do we then have a collection of documentation at tiles 30 through to 32 concerning the administration or the
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: prescription of and administration of two antibiotics, benzylpenicillin and gentamicin?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At 33 and 34 do we have the observations and the neonatal fluid balance chart, completed by Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Then at 35, do we have, timed at 15.45, a record of some swabs that were taken for pathology?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Again, a record made by Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At 36, timed at 16.00 hours, together with 37 at the same time, do we have vital signs and the fluid balance chart records?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Also at 16.00 hours at 38, a blood gas record?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Do we see here that the blood sugar of [Baby L] had certainly normalised to 5.8?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At 39 is there a retrospective nursing note which was actually written at 17.42 but you've put into the timeline at this stage because of its context?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Could you tell us what Lucy Letby wrote was going on at about this time?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: She writes:
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: "Subsequent blood sugars have been 2.5 micromoles and 5.8 micromoles with enteral feeds well tolerated, however she has advised to continue with this regime and wean. 10% glucose now at 2ml/kg/hour via peripheral line."
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Does that really take on from the previous tile 13, which refers to the registrar, Dr Bhowmik?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: So it would have to be read in that context, so "she"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: in that context is Dr Bhowmik?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At tile 40, is that a pathology sample taken at 16.46?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Then at 41, do we have the neonatal fluid balance chart first?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Then at 42, Dr Bhowmik's record or the time that Dr Bhowmik made her record concerning the material that is contained at tile 28 that we've already dealt with?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At tile 43 do we then have, first, the time that Lucy Letby was making the notes that we have previously referred to?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: But also some further information that she recorded that you have put in at this stage of the chronology?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Could you just deal with what Lucy Letby wrote at this time that's not already been dealt with?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Attended delivery of [Babies L & M] at 33 plus 2 weeks' gestation. Planned section for IUGR and oligohydramnios of twin 1. Times 2 steroids given. Born in condition (see medical notes). Brought to unit at 10.30. Initially had some
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: recession with a raised respiratory rate. Quickly normalised and has remained self-ventilating in air. Blood gases good."
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Then there's the records that we have dealt with on the two previous tiles. It then goes on to read:
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: "Two-hourly feeds (NG/bottle). Minimal aspirates obtained. Abdomen soft and non-distended. Urine and meconium passed.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Observations as charted. Incubator temperature reduced. SBR taken on gas machine and low reading given. Bloods obtained for septic screen due to early jaundice in twin 2 and lab result noted to be on treatment line, therefore phototherapy commenced. Eye protection in place. Antibiotics given as prescribed. Male infant [Surname of Babies L & M] alert and active."
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: In that context SBR is serum bilirubin, I think?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: All to do with jaundice.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: At 44, is there a note made 5 minutes after the previous note concerning communications that Lucy Letby had had with [Parents of Babies L & M]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Could you deal with those, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Introduced myself to parents prior to delivery. Parents had cuddles with both babies in theatre and photographs taken. Parents updated by myself on CLS and photograph given. Daddy has visited and had cuddles with male infant [Surname of Babies L & M]. Fully updated on care by myself and Reg Bhowmik. Aware of need for septic screen, IV fluids, NG tube feeds and phototherapy. Consent obtained for donor milk. Visiting hours discussed. A Davies has updated parents this evening."
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: A Davies presumably is Amy Davies.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Yes, thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: At 45 and 46, timed at 18.00 hours, do we have [Baby L]'s vital signs recorded together with the data on the neonatal fluid balance chart?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At the same time, tile 47, is there a blood gas record which, amongst other things, records [Baby L]'s blood sugar level?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Which was 3.3?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Then at 18.15, tile 48, did Lucy Letby send a message to [Nurse E]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Can you deal with the contents of that, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It reads:
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: "Unpacking. Stuff everywhere lol. May do extra shift over weekend."
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Is that then followed by social messaging for the next 3 minutes or so involving Lucy Letby on one part and [Nurse E] and [Nurse A] on the other?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At tile 50, is that the hourly, on the hour, at this stage, 19.00 hours, neonatal fluid balance chart data record?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At 51, at 19.20 hours, was there an outgoing text message sent by Lucy Letby to Susan Letby, her mother?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. It reads:
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: "Think I'm going to do tomorrow as an extra but go in a bit later. Extra money and Sat pay."
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: As in Saturday.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Yes. Did her mum respond almost immediately with "Great"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Was the care of [Baby L] handed over to Nurse Tracey Jones?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: We then move on to the night shift, which followed [Baby L]'s admission to the neonatal unit at tile 54 at 8 o'clock. And 55 and 56, do we have records of [Baby L]'s vital signs together with the fluid balance data?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Do we see that [Baby L]'s blood sugar was dipping a bit at tile 56, down to 2.3?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At tile 57, on 8 April still, timed at 21.04, did Sophie Ellis send a message to Lucy Letby asking:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "How's the house, pal?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Did Lucy Letby respond in the succeeding tile at 21.24?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. She responds with:
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: "Hey. It feels a bit weird having a whole house but it's good, thanks. Although stuff everywhere as moved in properly on Tuesday and been at work Wednesday, Thursday and today. Doing tomorrow as an extra so I'll see you tomorrow night. Won't be such an early start for you now back in Chester. Did I hear your grandparents are coming to see you?"
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Thank you. Did Sophie Ellis respond:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Yeah, I bet it does. It'll feel more homely once you've sorted everything out. Jeez, four LDs in a row. Are you okay?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's long days presumably in that context:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I know, yay, and I don't have to pay for petrol. It's costing me a fortune. Yeah, they are. Haven't seen them for a while. What's the unit like?"
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Did Lucy Letby respond to that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes:
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: "Yeah, I'll get there in time. Petrol and tunnel soon mounts up, doesn't it? Can you claim travel expenses? I couldn't for 405. Unit is busy. No one particularly unwell, just volume and few people off sick. I prefer 4 days to 4 nights. Least tomorrow is an extra and Sat pay. Aw, that'll be nice. Hope weather is a bit better for you."
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Thank you. Did Sophie Ellis respond:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Yeah, we can. OMG, really? How come? That's 7 weeks as well, isn't it? Yeah, 4 nights are awful. That's not too bad then.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Think I'd prefer to keep busy. I think it's meant to rain, damn it"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Is there then another message sent by Lucy Letby about 7 minutes later to Sophie Ellis?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that reads:
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: "Eirian said something about the induction being paid for by the trust, whereas the 405 comes out of network budget so won't pay as it's an expected part of role to progress, et cetera. Mad really and costs a bomb. We've got a nice mix of babies at the mo really. Shift goes quick anyway. Grr, typical April showers, ha ha. [Nurse E] is in Thailand and it has been 44 degrees today. "
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Did she then follow that up with a message to [Nurse E] in Thailand?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, saying:
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: "Your painting is finished. Got soaked walking home from work. Doing tomorrow as an extra now. Few more pennies."
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Do we then see at 64, 65 and 66, all timed at 22.00 hours, the record of [Baby L]'s vital signs together with the data on the fluid balance chart, which included the fact that [Baby L]'s blood sugar was low at 2.2?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, but tile 66 is actually 23.00.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: I beg your pardon. Sorry, it's my eyesight. Let's just rewind then.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So 64 and 65 are the 22.00 hours material that we've spoken of, the fact that [Baby L]'s blood sugar was low at 2.2?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: And recorded in brackets after that reading is "pre", and does that refer to pre-feed?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I presume so, yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: And 66, as you have rightly pointed out, is the same neonatal fluid balance chart filled in an hour later at 23.00 hours?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At 67, at 23.55, was a pathology sample taken, and the objective was to determine [Baby L]'s bilirubin level?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At 68, at midnight, just turning into Saturday, 9 April 2016, were [Baby L]'s vital signs recorded together with in the next tile, 69, at the same time, the data on the fluid balance chart?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Which included the fact that his, that is [Baby L]'s, blood sugar had risen to 3.6, which is within the acceptable range?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Another neonatal fluid balance chart an hour later at 01.00 hours?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Followed by observations and a neonatal fluid balance chart at tiles 71 and 72 respectively, both, as I have said, at 02.00 hours?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At 73, is there a record on the neonatal fluid balance chart of the fact that [Baby L]'s cannula had fallen out?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Then at 74, a prescription for benzylpenicillin?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Timed at 03.41?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At 75, timed at 03.41 as well, a prescription for sodium chloride?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: Then at 76 and 77, the observation chart followed by the neonatal fluid balance chart, timed at 04.00 hours?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: At 78, at 04.27 hours, have you transcribed Nurse Tracey Jones' nursing note?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TYNDALL

blocks.text: And has she -- can you take us through what she has recorded, please?

blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I am married to [Father of Babies L & M] and I am mum to [Baby L] and [Baby M]. I have been asked about my pregnancy with the boys and our time at the Countess of Chester Hospital.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "It was a routine pregnancy and I had no health issues until March of 2016 when I began to feel unwell and had to go for a scan. On that day, the doctor said to me and my husband that I was not well and I needed to be admitted straightaway. We were both surprised and shocked.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I was admitted to the hospital. That night, a nurse said that they had to give me a steroid injection and I think in the end I had three or four injections. I stayed for 15 or 17 days. They asked if I wanted to have a natural labour or a C-section. I asked the nurse when they were going to do the operation and they said they had looked through my file and were worried, so it would be early the next morning at 9 am.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "The next morning was Friday, 8 April 2016. When I got to the theatre, two nurses from the neonatal unit were also there, Lucy
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: and Laura. Laura introduced herself and Lucy and said that they were there to take the babies into an intercare room if the twins were poorly. The C-section was fine and the boys were delivered.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "They were 33 weeks old and both weighed 3 pounds. The doctor said that they were very healthy and very nice. They asked if I wanted a picture and they put them in my arms and I had a picture with them.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "At 12 noon on 9 April, my husband's parents and family came to see us and they were taken through to the neonatal unit to see the boys. We went downstairs from my ward to see them. They were in the first room. I was happy and we were chatting to each other.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I had a photograph of the boys next to my bed and at that time we hadn't decided what they were going to be called. It was a week later when we decided on [Baby L] and [Baby M].
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "About 10 minutes after we left the boys, a nurse called Yvonne came running up. She said I had to go back down and took me down in the wheelchair. I asked why and she said she would explain downstairs.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "When we got there, one of the doctors was just pressing [Baby M]'s chest. People were saying that the boys were healthy yesterday and they didn't know what had happened today. One of the nurses, with glasses and a bob haircut, said she'd done everything with him and he was absolutely good and she didn't know what had happened.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I don't know her name but it sounded like she was the nurse in charge of his care. She was short and fair. I was praying to my god to see my boy and help him because I have never done anything wrong to other people, I was asking my God to save him. My husband was not saying anything and was crying and crying. [Baby L] was okay on the other side of the room.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Lucy was there with Laura and the nurse in glasses with the bob haircut was there too. The doctor was black and wore glasses, I think. My mind was totally blank other than praying to my god.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Then it seemed, after hours, they said I should go back to my room as he had stabilised. They couldn't give us any explanation as to why it had happened. At the time I didn't want to discuss it with them so I went back to my room.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Then when I was discharged after 2 weeks, the boys stayed in their intercare room. From the Saturday that [Baby M] was really poorly, both boys were really stable and there weren't any other
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: problems. Whilst I was in hospital, I would manage to walk down to the unit every day and spend all day with the boys and my husband would come after work.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "After I was discharged, I would still go and see them every day. My boys were discharged in May after about 3 or 4 weeks of being there. They hadn't put a lot of weight on, but were both fit and well and everything was fine. When we left hospital, the boys were very small.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Since being discharged, [Baby M] has had scans and we have been told that there were no after-effects of what happened to him. We've been assured everything is clear."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Witness statement of [FATHER OF BABIES L & M] (read)
I then turn to her husband's statement, which is at page 3, my Lord, the statement of [Father of Babies L & M] dated 5 March 2020. He identifies himself and says:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I am married to [Mother of Babies L & M] and we have two boys, [Baby L] and [Baby M], who were born at the Countess of Chester on 8 April 2016.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Up until March 2016, it had been a routine pregnancy and we had found out early on that we were having twins after a scan. blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "After doing their checks, they told us that they would have to admit her as soon as possible, which I think was down to the position the boys were in. blocks.text: "[Mother of Babies L & M] decided on a C-section and they agreed to do that. I was with her when they were born and we got to see them straightaway and the doctors said they were very healthy. blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I was able to go down to the unit a couple of hours later to see the boys while my wife had to stay upstairs. I can't remember who was looking after them when I went down, but they were both still fine and in nursery 1.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "The next day my parents and my brother and sister-in-law went into the hospital with me to go and see [Mother of Babies L & M] and meet the boys in the neonatal unit. We went upstairs to the ward first to see her and then we all went down to the unit with [Mother of Babies L & M] to see the boys for about half an hour or so. We were both proud parents and very happy.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "We then went back upstairs to the ward. Within 10 minutes of being on the ward, a nurse came charging in saying, 'You need to come down now'. I can't remember which nurse it was or what she looked like. So we all rushed downstairs.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I was down first as [Mother of Babies L & M] was being pushed in her wheelchair and I saw one of the doctors doing chest compressions on [Baby M]. It was very distressing to see and I will never forget that image. I still have it in my mind.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "[Mother of Babies L & M] and the others arrived shortly after me and one of the nurses said that [Baby M] had been absolutely fine and they didn't know what had happened to him. [Baby L] was on the other side of the room and was fine. I remember they were working on [Baby M] for half an hour and they later told us his heart had stopped. He then stabilised, he had come round, and his colour started coming back.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "After that, my wife stayed in hospital for about 2 weeks. During that time, both boys were stable and I would visit them every day. [Mother of Babies L & M] would spend time with them during the day and I would go to the hospital on my way home from work at 4 pm to spend time with them.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Once [Mother of Babies L & M] had been discharged, she would go on the bus every day to the hospital and spend most of the day with the boys. There weren't any other issues with the boys and it was actually only [Baby M] who had the problem early on. The only thing [Baby M] had to have was a brain scan to make sure there were no problems after his resuscitation, but the scan showed nothing of concern, no damage.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "The boys were discharged in early May, I think after being there for 3 or 4 weeks. They were only on the unit because they didn't weigh enough, but other than that they were both healthy. They were fit and well when they were released and it was a relief to finally get the boys home. We are happy with the development of both boys at this point."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: bit slower to crying, he was rubbed down a bit with a towel and he began crying and he was fine. Few babies achieve an Apgar score of 10 at 1 minute as they are often a bit blue at birth, so a score of 9 is good.

blocks.text: "The births were perfect, the only issue being I have noted from the notes entered by the paediatrician that [Baby M] had oxygen saturations of 60% at 3 minutes, which is a little low, but this was corrected by the administration of inflation breaths.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I had no further involvement with [Baby M] and I did not hear of his collapse the following day."
